stem.en: Why is it useful for a eukaryotic cell to have organelles?

text.en: Organelles make the cell much smaller, which lets water enter more quickly from outside.

feedback.en: Organelles do not make a cell smaller. Eukaryotic cells are usually larger than prokaryotic cells.

text.en: Every organelle does exactly the same job, so a damaged one can be replaced by any other.

feedback.en: Each organelle does a specific job. They are not all alike.

text.en: Different processes can run at the same time.
Organelles do the thinking for the cell and plan out which of its jobs should be done first.

feedback.en: Organelles do not think or plan. They carry out processes.

explanation.en: Eukaryotic cells carry out various life processes in different organelles, independently and at the same time.

hints.en: What does each organelle do, and when?
